notes:
I couldn't do any research for Numbers 24, so I have no notes to give you. The first time I tried to search, I got the message "You have no more code_execution tool calls remaining this turn." That tool is the only one that reaches the internet, so I couldn't open any of the approved sites (Enduring Word, Bible Hub, StudyLight, Precept Austin, the NET Bible notes, New Advent and the rest).

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I read no pages, any notes I wrote now would break all three rules, so I've stopped here.

**Next step:** ask again in a new turn, when the limit should have reset. I would then:
1. Read the verse-by-verse commentaries on Numbers 24: Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub or StudyLight, Precept Austin, and Wesley's notes.
2. Look up the verses that come up most in debate:
   - **v. 2:** what it means that "the Spirit of God came upon" Balaam, and whether he was a true prophet. Pentecostal, Wesleyan and Reformed teachers may answer differently.
   - **v. 7:** the king "greater than Agag."
   - **v. 17:** the "star from Jacob," read as pointing to David, to the Messiah, or to the Magi's star. Catholic and Orthodox sources take this up too.
   - **vv. 22–24:** the predictions about Asshur, Eber and the ships from Cyprus, using the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey.
3. Write the notes verse by verse ("v. 4: …") with a URL after each point, and leave out anything I can't find.

If it would help, I could cover verses 1–14 in one turn and 15–25 in the next.
